methodological_rigor.justification: The design is appropriate for a first-in-human phase 1 trial: 3+3 dose escalation (parts A1/A2) with Bayesian-monitored dose expansion (part B), appropriate GCP oversight (IRBs at 22 sites, data review committee), and prespecified eligibility criteria for ICI-resistant disease. However, the trial is single-arm with no control, expansion cohort sizes are small (n=11 per cohort except ccRCC n=30), and biomarker analyses rely on empirically-determined cutoffs (acknowledged) with very small sample sizes (e.g., n=3 PR, n=5 SD, n=5 PD for Treg/CD8 ratios in Fig. 3c). Figure 3 explicitly notes 'single technical replicate per sample' for biomarker assays, a limitation for reproducibility. Statistical treatment is adequate but basic: descriptive statistics, Clopper–Pearson exact 95% CIs for ORRs, Kaplan–Meier for DOR/PFS; no multiplicity correction is applied across the multiple biomarker cutoff explorations in ccRCC, and no formal power calculation is reported (appropriate for phase 1 but the inferential biomarker claims warrant caveats).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual non-randomized phase 1 interventional cohort (single-arm, open-label), which maps to Oxford LoE 2b (low-quality cohort/early-phase trial without randomization). Clinical relevance is high: the study addresses the major unmet need of anti-PD-1 resistance across four tumor types, demonstrates a manageable safety profile for a first-in-class selective latent TGFβ1 antibody that avoids the cardiotoxicity of pan-TGFβ inhibitors, and reports clinically meaningful ORR (20% in heavily pretreated ccRCC with intermediate/poor IMDC prognosis) and DOR (median 10.6 months for ccRCC) in a population where ICI retreatment typically yields single-digit responses. The biomarker-based patient selection strategy (CD8+ T cells, Treg cells, TGFB1 expression) is a plausible translational path to a companion diagnostic for a phase 2 trial that is said to be in development.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this early-phase trial. The manuscript reports eligibility criteria in detail, provides a CONSORT diagram (Fig. 1), lists all protocol amendments (five amendments with rationale), discloses prespecified primary/secondary/exploratory objectives, provides protocol registration (NCT04291079), and reports TRAEs/SAEs/discontinuations with grading per CTCAE v5.0. Minor gaps include incomplete reporting of per-site enrollment numbers and limited detail on dose-escalation decisions. Data and code availability information was redacted/blinded ('Online content' points to a redacted link), so based on what remains the sharing posture cannot be positively verified; no explicit mention of deposited raw data, biomarker datasets, or analysis code.

novelty_literature.justification: The study presents the first-in-human clinical experience of a first-in-class selective anti-latent TGFβ1 monoclonal antibody that specifically targets context-independent latent TGFβ1 while sparing TGFβ2/TGFβ3 — a conceptually and methodologically novel approach that circumvents the cardiotoxicity that has derailed prior pan-TGFβ and TGFβR1 inhibitors (e.g., bintrafusp alfa, galunisertib). The combination with pembrolizumab in heavily pretreated ICI-resistant ccRCC is a novel setting, and biomarker correlations supporting a Treg/TGFB1-based selection strategy add originality. Novelty is tempered by the fact that TGFβ+ICI combinations have been explored extensively (Mariathasan 2018, Tauriello 2018, bintrafusp alfa trials) and the isoform-selective concept was already demonstrated in preclinical work by Martin et al. 2020 — this is the clinical translation of a published concept rather than conceptual first-in-class.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear flow from background (TGFβ biology and ICI resistance), through study design, to results segmented by trial part, and a substantive discussion that explicitly acknowledges limitations (single-arm design, heavily pretreated population, empirical biomarker cutoffs, small sample sizes). The abstract is quantitatively grounded with specific ORRs by tumor type. Table and figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, with sample sizes clearly stated. Minor issues: embedded table text runs together in the markdown rendering, some discussion sections rehash results (e.g., ORR percentages restated multiple times), and the Main/Introduction section is positioned after Discussion which disrupts normal flow (likely a markdown artifact of the Nature Portfolio online format).

key_strengths: First-in-human phase 1 trial of a first-in-class selective anti-latent TGFβ1 antibody avoiding the cardiotoxicity that derailed pan-TGFβ inhibitors

Clinically meaningful 20% confirmed ORR with 10.6-month median DOR in heavily pretreated anti-PD-1-resistant ccRCC (29/30 patients with intermediate/poor IMDC prognosis), where ICI retreatment typically yields single-digit responses
Mechanistic biomarker data (CD8+ infiltration, Treg/CD8 ratio, gMDSC suppression, baseline TGFB1) support both proof-of-mechanism and a plausible ccRCC patient-selection strategy
Rigorous multicenter trial conduct across 22 sites with IRB oversight, data review committee, five transparently reported protocol amendments, and detailed CONSORT-style flow
key_concerns: Single-arm, open-label design with no control arm; efficacy signals must be interpreted against historical expectations rather than randomized comparator

Biomarker cutoffs for CD8+/Treg/TGFB1 are empirically derived in very small subgroups (n=14–16 ccRCC biopsies) with no multiplicity correction across multiple explored thresholds — risk of post hoc overfitting for the proposed selection strategy
Expansion cohort sizes for non-ccRCC tumor types are small (n=11 each), yielding wide CIs; ORRs of 9.1% in HNSCC/urothelial are based on single responders
Biomarker assays reported as single technical replicate per sample (Fig. 3 caption), limiting internal replication rigor
Data and code availability information is redacted in the blinded version and cannot be positively verified from the remaining text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound and transparently reported first-in-human phase 1 trial of a genuinely first-in-class selective latent TGFβ1 inhibitor with a clinically meaningful efficacy signal in anti-PD-1-resistant ccRCC and manageable safety — appropriate for a top-tier oncology/translational venue with minor revisions to clarify multiplicity in biomarker analyses and data-sharing posture.
